findings.title: A profile switch, copy or reset leaves elements placed by the OLD profile, because Anchor reads the features' cached cfg upvalues in an undefined bus dispatch order
findings.locations: modules/Anchor.lua:359; modules/Anchor.lua:123-124 (wrong comment); modules/CastBars.lua:372,408; modules/TargetFrames.lua:258,297; modules/PetFrames.lua:139,178; tests/test_anchor.lua:181-182 (wrong comment); libs/CallbackHandler-1.0/CallbackHandler-1.0.lua:16
findings.evidence: CallbackHandler dispatches with next(), so the order of PROFILE handlers is hash order, not TOC order. spec.config returns a captured cfg upvalue that each feature rebinds only in its own PROFILE handler. Nothing re-anchors afterwards. Reproduced in a scratch script: 'back to Default pet anchoredToHolder=true cfgMode=attached' and 'after Reset all settings target anchoredToHolder=true cfgMode=attached'. The comments at Anchor.lua:123-124 and test_anchor.lua:181-182 wrongly assume registration order equals dispatch order.
findings.remediation: C-001 / T-1: change spec.config to read live data (`function() return NS.db.profile.castbar|target|pet end`) in all three features, and switch the slotSize closures to the same live read. Rewrite the Anchor comment to say CallbackHandler order is undefined. Add real-switch tests to tests/test_anchor.lua (or a new tests/test_profile_switch.lua): SetProfile between profiles that differ in anchorMode, assert __aTarget, repeat after RestoreAllDefaults. Mark the case with `-- red under: revert config() to the captured upvalue`. Rejected: deferring to the next frame, or a second ordered PROFILE message.
findings.verify_reason: Anchor.lua:359 re-applies on MSG.PROFILE through spec.config(), which is `function() return cfg end` over an upvalue rebound only in each feature's own PROFILE handler (CastBars.lua:372/406-408, TargetFrames.lua:258/296-298, PetFrames.lua:139/177-179). CallbackHandler Dispatch (CallbackHandler-1.0.lua:16-22) walks handlers with next() over a table keyed by target, and every receiver has its own NS.NewBusTarget() table, so dispatch order is hash order, not TOC order. The feature handlers' reconfigure/reskin/refresh never call Anchor.Apply, and Providers' PROFILE burst sends LAYOUT only when the frame map changed (Providers.lua:230-237), so nothing re-anchors afterwards. The comments at Anchor.lua:119-126 and test_anchor.lua:178-183 do assume registration order equals dispatch order. The remediation (a live NS.db.profile read in config and slotSize, keeping the shipped-default fallback in placementOf) is sound. High stands: placement stays wrong after a routine profile switch, copy or reset until a reload or an unrelated LAYOUT/CONFIG.

findings.title: `/pfe profile new <existing name>` silently wipes that profile and prints 'Created' (data loss)
findings.evidence: `new` calls db:SetProfile(name) and then NS.ResetProfileCounted(db) without checking whether the name already exists. Reproduced: profile new Healer, set castbar.width 222, profile use Default, profile new Healer; castbar.width comes back as 140. The case meets the Critical floor; the review graded it High because it needs a name collision, and triage may raise it.
findings.remediation: C-002 / T-2: add an exists(db,name) helper based on db:GetProfiles(). `new` refuses an existing name with one tagged, localized line pointing at use/reset. Add a test in tests/test_slash.lua (`-- red under: drop the exists() guard in new`). Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit.
findings.verify_reason: Slash.lua:270-274: `new` calls db:SetProfile(name) and then NS.ResetProfileCounted(db) with no existence check, so an existing profile is switched to, wiped and reported as 'Created'. That is silent loss of a whole profile's data from one ordinary command. The rule refs exist (slash-commands §3/§4, localization §1/§5). The remediation (an exists() guard via db:GetProfiles(), a localized refusal and a red-under test) is correct.

findings.title: The stand-down leaves the EditMode.Exit EventRegistry callback registered, and burst() keeps arming two C_Timer.After timers while the addon is disabled
findings.evidence: `pcall(EventRegistry.RegisterCallback, EventRegistry, "EditMode.Exit", burst, Providers)` is registered once in OnEnable. Suspend runs only ev:UnregisterAllEvents(). burst() bumps burstGen and arms two C_Timer.After calls even while suspended. The callback has a real unregister, so the hooksecurefunc carve-out does not apply. The audit graded this Medium (MUST).
findings.remediation: C-004 / T-4 / audit Sprint 1.4: add a registerEditMode(on) or registerCallbacks()/unregisterCallbacks() pair behind the presence guard and pcall. Call it from OnEnable/Resume, and call the unregister from Suspend. burst() returns before it touches burstGen or timers while suspended. Add `-- red under: drop unregisterCallbacks() from Providers:Suspend` / `-- red under: drop the suspended guard in burst`. Rejected: an addon-side tracked-callback helper, which would be a second stand-down record (anti-pattern #85). If one is wanted, it belongs as a LibKa0s Bus minor.
findings.verify_reason: Real as stated. Providers.lua:341-344 registers the EventRegistry 'EditMode.Exit' callback once, in OnEnable. Suspend (348-353) only runs ev:UnregisterAllEvents(), and burst() (61-67) arms two C_Timer.After timers with no suspended check. slash-commands §7 says the hooksecurefunc carve-out MUST NOT be generalized to anything that has a real unregister. Severity is lowered because of what can actually be reached. The PROFILE message path is stood down by the bus record, so the only live trigger is leaving Edit Mode while disabled. Each trigger arms two one-shot timers that end in Providers.Request(), which returns at once because `suspended` is set (line 54). No drawing, no SV write, and the cost is negligible. It is a conformance gap, not user-visible harm. The remediation is otherwise correct: use EventRegistry:UnregisterCallback('EditMode.Exit', Providers) in Suspend and re-register in Resume, both behind the existing presence guard and pcall, and have burst() return early while suspended.

findings.title: The secure-write memo compares against the APPLIED value, so a change reverted in combat is lost (Click to target stays off after combat)
findings.evidence: `if btn.__clicks == on then return end` and `if btn.__driver == driver then return end` are set only inside the deferred closure. Toggling A→B→A in combat therefore leaves B queued. Reproduced: 'setting true btn.__clicks false attr *type1 nil' after leaving combat.
findings.remediation: C-003 / T-3: keep request-side memos (__clicksWant, __driverWant) that are set at request time and used for the early return. __clicks/__driver stay as the applied state inside the closure. Test in tests/test_targetframes.lua (and petframes): force InCombatLockdown, toggle clickToTarget false then true, call OnLeaveCombat, and assert *type1 == 'target'. Mark it `-- red under: compare against btn.__clicks`.
findings.verify_reason: UnitButtons.lua:52-68: ApplyDriver and ApplyClicks early-return on btn.__driver/__clicks, which are set only inside the deferred RunSecure closure. NS.RunSecure (core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:62-72) queues the latest write per key in combat. So applied=true, then toggle false (queued), then toggle true returns early because __clicks is still true, and the queued false is flushed on PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED. The setting reads on while the button is click-dead, which is reachable in normal play. The request-side memo remediation is correct. Clearing or overwriting the pending key on the early-return path would be an equivalent fix.

findings.title: Profile sub-verbs mishandle bad names: copy raises a raw AceDB error, delete of a missing profile prints a false 'Deleted', and use of a typo silently creates a profile
findings.evidence: db:CopyProfile raises 'Cannot copy profile %q as it does not exist.' and 'Cannot have the same source and destination profiles'. delete passes silent=true and prints 'Deleted profile X' for a profile that does not exist. SetProfile creates a profile on demand, so a mistyped `use` creates one. The kit's AceDB fake hides the copy error (F-011).
findings.remediation: C-002 / T-2: use, copy and delete refuse a missing name, and copy also refuses the current profile. Each refusal is one tagged, localized line through the existing printer; format strings go in locales/enUS.lua. Add tests for each verb to tests/test_slash.lua. The copy test goes red only after the F-011 kit re-vendor; until then, assert on the printed line. Note in the changelog that `use` no longer creates profiles. Rejected: pcall-and-print of the AceDB error.
findings.verify_reason: Slash.lua:275-285: `copy` calls db:CopyProfile(name) unguarded, and AceDB-3.0.lua:581-587 raises both 'Cannot have the same source and destination profiles' and 'Cannot copy profile %q as it does not exist.' as raw Lua errors from a slash command. `delete` passes silent=true and always prints 'Deleted profile'. `use` goes through SetProfile, which creates profiles on demand. The kit fake at tests/_kit/mock_record.lua:257-259 silently returns on both copy error cases, so it hides the raise. That is correctly routed as a separate LibKa0s kit finding and not edited locally. The fix is addon-side in Slash.lua, and nothing is proposed for libs/AceDB-3.0. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: The stand-down replaces the target and pet buttons' secure state drivers with 'hide' instead of unregistering them
findings.evidence: Driver returns 'hide' when not allowed, and ApplyDriver re-registers it, so ten state drivers stay registered while the addon is disabled. UnregisterStateDriver is declared in .luacheckrc but never called. slash-commands-§7 requires state drivers to be stood down where they can be, which is out of combat.
findings.remediation: C-005 / T-5, after T-3 and T-1: while suspended, refresh calls UnitButtons.Release(btn). Through NS.RunSecure('driver:'..key) it runs UnregisterStateDriver(btn,'visibility'), btn:Hide() and clears __driver, and it sets __driverWant=nil at request time. Stand-up re-registers through refresh. Add tests in tests/test_disabled.lua: no __drivers.visibility after an out-of-combat disable, re-enable restores the driver, and the in-combat variant completes after OnLeaveCombat. Mark them `-- red under: keep the "hide" driver`. Needs a combat smoke test (S-005).
findings.verify_reason: Real. TargetFrames.lua:185-188 (and the PetFrames equivalent) compute allowed=false while suspended, and UnitButtons.Driver returns 'hide', which ApplyDriver registers with RegisterStateDriver. The ten state drivers therefore stay registered while the addon is disabled, and UnregisterStateDriver is never called anywhere (only declared at .luacheckrc:31). slash-commands §7 explicitly says secure state drivers are stood down where they can be, and deferred out of combat. Severity is lowered for impact: a constant 'hide' driver only costs the secure state-driver manager's periodic evaluation of ten trivial conditions. Nothing is drawn or written and the player sees nothing. It is a MUST conformance gap with negligible reachable cost. The remediation (a Release through NS.RunSecure that unregisters, hides, clears __driver and resets the request memo from R-04) is correct. Its ordering after R-04 is right because it depends on the __driverWant memo.

findings.title: The zero-overhead perf scenario compares capture-off with capture-on instead of with instrumentation absent
findings.evidence: `assert_(probeOff.bytesPerIter <= probeOn.bytesPerIter + 1, ...)` would pass a dormant bracket that allocates as much as an armed one. The probeOverheadOff ≤ 24 B ceiling only partly compensates. Today: off 0.0 B/iter, on 0.5 B/iter.
findings.remediation: Build a true 'absent' baseline and do not compare against castStartStop. Preferred: load a second environment where NS.Perf is pre-seeded so the bracket compiles to nothing, or where the bracket helpers are stubbed out, then measure castOnce there and assert probeOff.bytesPerIter <= absent.bytesPerIter + 1. Acceptable fallback: wrap debugprofilestop and NS.Perf.Note with call counters, assert 0 calls per iteration while Perf.on == false, and keep the existing ceiling. Add a comment explaining why this stands in for 'absent'. Add no wall-clock assertion. It stays a scenario outside docs/test-cases.md.
findings.verify_reason: Real. tests/perf.lua:234-240 compares capture-off with capture-on, but performance §9 requires the zero-overhead scenario to pin capture-off against the same path 'with the instrumentation absent'. Severity is lowered: tests/perf.lua is a measurement runner outside the green gate (testing §7). Today's figures show off=0.0 B/iter, and the 24 B probeOverheadOff ceiling already bounds it, so this is missing evidence rather than a shipped regression. The remediation's 'practical alternative' is also flawed. `probeOff.bytesPerIter <= castStartStop.bytesPerIter + 1` compares capture-off against another capture-off measurement (Perf.on is false at perf.lua:173). castStartStop also runs FIVE start/stop cycles per iteration against castOnce's one, and measures 16.6 B/iter, so the bound is about 16 B looser than intended and not an 'absent' baseline at all.

findings.title: No test covers a real profile switch or the profile sub-verbs, so the suite stays green over two High bugs
findings.evidence: test_database calls NS.OnProfileChanged() directly and never checks placement. test_slash covers only `profile` with no argument. F-001, F-002, F-003 (the profile route) and F-004 go undetected.
findings.remediation: Track no separate work. Close this finding when the red-first tests from R-01 (a real SetProfile, CopyProfile and reset placement), R-02 and R-05 (every profile sub-verb) and R-04 (the in-combat A-to-B-to-A toggle, not a profile route) land. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commits.
findings.verify_reason: The gap is real. tests/test_database.lua:38-43 calls NS.OnProfileChanged() directly and asserts only message counts. tests/test_slash.lua:98-100 covers only a bare `profile`. The SetProfile calls in test_launcher.lua:181-183 and test_optionssetup.lua:216-217 never assert placement or sub-verb output. It is a roll-up of the coverage gaps behind R-01, R-02, R-04 and R-05, and its remediation is fully the red-first tests those findings already specify. It needs no separate work item, so severity is lowered to low to avoid counting the same defects twice. One correction: F-003/R-04 is the in-combat toggle route, not a profile route, so the test it needs is the combat A-to-B-to-A toggle case, not a profile switch.

findings.title: The test kit's AceDB fake does not raise on CopyProfile/DeleteProfile the way AceDB-3.0 does, and does not strip defaults from the outgoing profile on SetProfile
findings.evidence: `if not src or name == current then return end` returns silently where AceDB raises. DeleteProfile is silent on the current profile. SetProfile never runs removeDefaults. This breaks kit fidelity rule 5 ('Model the awkward real behavior') and hides F-004 and stripped-default reads in every consumer.
findings.remediation: Upstream U-1: in LibKa0s testkit/mock_record.lua, CopyProfile raises the AceDB messages. DeleteProfile raises on the active profile, and on a missing one unless silent. SetProfile strips defaults from the outgoing profile. Bump the kit revision with a README entry. Then re-vendor the whole tests/_kit and libs/LibKa0s into this addon and every consumer, one commit each. Other consumers may go red, which is expected. Never edit it locally.
findings.verify_reason: tests/_kit/mock_record.lua:241-246 SetProfile only swaps and fires, with no removeDefaults. :258-265 CopyProfile has `if not src or name == current then return end`. :267-270 DeleteProfile silently returns on the current profile and silently deletes a missing one. The vendored AceDB-3.0 raises in each of these cases: CopyProfile :581-587 on the same or a missing profile unless silent, DeleteProfile :531-537 on the active profile or a missing one unless silent, and SetProfile :460-463 calls removeDefaults(oldProfile). The kit's own header rule 5 (mock_base.lua:26, 'Model the awkward real behavior') is broken. Because of this, PFE's F-004 (settings/Slash.lua profile copy raising a raw Lua error) cannot be reproduced headlessly. The Medium grade is the test-inventory cap, and it is justified because the gap hides a reachable defect. The file is kit-owned, so it routes upstream to LibKa0s with a whole-folder re-vendor.

findings.title: The test kit has no EventRegistry fake or recorder, so test_disabled cannot see the EditMode.Exit survivor
findings.locations: tests/_kit/mock_base.lua, tests/_kit/mock_record.lua (upstream testkit); tests/wow_mock.lua; modules/Providers.lua:342-345; tests/test_disabled.lua:95-97
findings.evidence: `grep EventRegistry tests/_kit/mock_base.lua tests/wow_mock.lua` returns nothing. The presence guard is false in the harness, so the callback never enters __registrations(), and step 3 of test_disabled cannot fail on PFE-12/F-005.
findings.remediation: Review (preferred): upstream U-2 adds an additive recording EventRegistry (RegisterCallback/UnregisterCallback/TriggerEvent, kind='callback' in __registrations()) to LibKa0s testkit/mock_base.lua and mock_record.lua, sharing the kit revision bump with U-1, then re-vendors tests/_kit whole. Audit (interim): add an EventRegistry recorder to the addon-owned tests/wow_mock.lua, and confirm step 3 goes red at 314c95e and green after the PFE-12 fix. The review says a test-local shim is acceptable until the kit ships one.
findings.verify_reason: A grep for EventRegistry across tests/ (kit and wow_mock.lua) returns nothing. modules/Providers.lua:342-345 registers EditMode.Exit only when the EventRegistry global exists, so the harness never records it. Providers:Suspend (:348-353) only calls ev:UnregisterAllEvents() and never unregisters the callback, so the survivor is real. test_disabled's regs() (:35-40) reads only mocks.__registrations(), so step 3 cannot see it. Low fits a test-coverage gap. Routing upstream as U-2 is correct. The interim addon-local shim in tests/wow_mock.lua is allowed because that file is addon-owned. One caveat: the shim has to feed whatever __registrations() reads, and that list is kit-owned. If the kit exposes no append hook, the interim shim has to be asserted separately in test_disabled.

findings.title: The library-absent Slash stub hand-copies LibKa0s's refusal-line format and row shape, and re-implements its dispatcher; slash-commands-§1 and §7 pull in opposite directions
findings.evidence: `local DISABLED_LINE = "%s is disabled \226\128\148 enable it with |cFFFFFF00%s|r"` copies lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT, and FormatRow copies `cmd — desc`. §1 says a stub MUST NOT re-implement the library's rendering, while §7 requires one collection-wide refusal line even in a degraded build. The parity test pins the drift. The review graded this Low; the audit filed it as Info because it is a question of how two rules interact.
findings.remediation: Upstream first. WowAddonStandards rules on the §1/§7 interaction: either slash-commands-§1 names the refusal line as the one string a library-absent stub may carry, or the rule requires LibKa0s to export the refusal shape as data that a host can bundle. LibKa0s documents the prescribed stub shape in its Slash docs 'Degradation' section. Addon side: now, drop the copied FormatRow em-dash formatter in favour of a plainly rendered row, and correct the false comment at settings/Slash.lua:322-324. Leave the DisabledLine wording alone until the standard rules, then adopt exactly what it prescribes. Do not invent a new per-addon refusal sentence. Adjust test_surface_parity to match the ruled shape.
findings.verify_reason: The evidence is accurate. settings/Slash.lua:327 copies the row formatter (`cmd .. ' — ' .. desc`). :331 copies lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT verbatim (libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:83). The comment at :322-324 ('No formatter ... is copied here') is false. slash-commands-§1 (lines 18-19) forbids a stub from copying the row formatter, but it also requires a stub carrying OnSlash, so a minimal stub dispatch is sanctioned rather than a hand-rolled dispatcher. §7's refusal-line rule (line 81) says the wording 'MUST NOT be re-spelled per addon'. The addon-side remediation, printing a plain '<brand> is disabled; /pfe enable turns it back on (LibKa0s missing)', is itself a per-addon re-spelling of the refusal line, so it would trade one §1/§7 deviation for a §7 deviation. The path is reachable only in a build missing LibKa0s, so Low stands.

findings.title: docs/performance.md figures are stale, and settingsDrag grew by about 50% without anyone noticing
findings.evidence: The doc says castStartStop 16.6 B/iter; measured today 5.4. The doc says settingsDrag 596 B/iter; measured today 895.9 (bundle 885.9). Probably caused by structureSignature (modules/Element.lua:168-176) gaining three marker fields. settingsDrag has no assertion.
findings.remediation: C-006 / T-7, after T-6: re-run tests/perf.lua and copy the figures into docs/performance.md in the same change, explain the settingsDrag growth, and update the perf.lua comment text without changing any ceiling. Never hand-edit a number that was not just measured.
findings.verify_reason: docs/performance.md:88 says castStartStop 16.6 B/iter, :92 says settingsDrag 596, and :95 dates the figures 2026-09-15. I re-ran lua5.1 tests/perf.lua today and got castStartStop 5.4 and settingsDrag 895.9, which match the finding. tests/perf.lua:243-258 comments still cite 16.6, and settingsDrag has no ceiling. The structureSignature explanation for the growth is unverified, so the remediation correctly asks for the cause to be established and explained. Docs drift with no runtime impact, so Low.

findings.title: .luacheckrc whitelists 12 globals that nothing uses, including the deliberately removed UnitExists
findings.evidence: GetTime, wipe, Mixin, UnitExists, UnitGUID, UnitIsUnit, UnitIsDeadOrGhost, UnitIsConnected, C_Secrets, RegisterUnitWatch, UnregisterUnitWatch and UnregisterStateDriver have 0 bare-global uses. A raw UnitExists(compoundToken) would lint clean, which is the secret-value hazard Compat documents removing.
findings.remediation: C-008 / T-9, after T-5: remove the unused names. UnregisterStateDriver stays because C-005 gives it a real use. Keep UnitExists out, with a comment pointing to core/Compat.lua:205-208.
findings.verify_reason: .luacheckrc:14-38 lists all 12 names. A grep over authored Lua (excluding libs/, tests/_kit/ and docs/) finds zero bare-global reads of any of them: the hits are comments or `mocks.X` field accesses (tests/test_providers.lua:68/142, tests/wow_mock.lua:130 `M.UnregisterStateDriver`, tests/test_targetframes.lua:166). core/Compat.lua:205-208 documents deliberately removing a UnitExists shim, so whitelisting UnitExists lets the hazard lint clean. Keeping UnregisterStateDriver depends on C-005, which is out of scope here. Removing it now is also lint-safe.

findings.title: Dead locale keys ('Position' and the old '/pfe %s does nothing while the addon is off' refusal) plus two near-duplicate key pairs
findings.evidence: 209 keys scanned. The :150 refusal key has no reader (both bundles). 'Position' is read only by a negative test (audit). The review's scan also found near-duplicates: 'All settings reset to defaults' vs '...defaults.', and the same split for 'Cannot reset settings…'. A player can see the wording drift.
findings.remediation: Delete the dead 'Position' and '/pfe %s does nothing while the addon is off …' keys (localization-§1: no key nothing reads). Collapse each near-duplicate pair to one spelling. No-trailing-period is the recommended choice for consistency with the collection's chat lines, but it is a preference, since slash-commands-§4 only forbids trailing colons. Delete the twin and point settings/General.lua:200/202 at the kept key. Optionally add a dead-key guard in tests. Sequence after PFE-17 as planned.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. locales/enUS.lua:31 'Position' is read only by tests/test_optionssetup.lua:88 (a negative assertion). The :150 '/pfe %s does nothing while the addon is off' key has no reader. The twin pairs sit at :134-136 and are read with a period at settings/General.lua:200/202 and without one at settings/Slash.lua:107/109. The L metatable falls back to the key (enUS.lua:11), so deleting 'Position' keeps the test resolving. The dead-key rule is localization-§1 (localization.md:67-69, which says enUS.lua MUST NOT accumulate keys nothing reads), not §3 (Coverage). slash-commands-§4 prescribes only 'no trailing colon'. 'No trailing period' appears only in the §7 refusal-line rule (slash-commands.md:254). Choosing the no-period spelling is a reasonable house preference, but no rule mandates it.

findings.title: The migration runner migrates only the active profile but stamps the account-wide schemaVersion
findings.evidence: `step.apply(NS.db.profile)` followed by `g.schemaVersion = step.to`. The first real ladder step would leave every non-active profile unmigrated forever. SCHEMA_STEPS is empty today, so nothing can reach it. Review graded Low; audit filed Info (an observation).
findings.remediation: Review C-008 / T-10 (fix now): apply each step to every stored profile (`for name,p in pairs(NS.db.profiles or {[cur]=NS.db.profile})`), with defaults-merge caveats commented, and stamp the global version only after all profiles. Add a unit case with a test-local injected fake step using two profiles. The audit's alternative is to defer until the first step is written, or to migrate lazily on OnProfileChanged with a per-profile stamp.
findings.verify_reason: core/Database.lua:37-48 runs step.apply(NS.db.profile), the active profile only, then stamps the account-wide g.schemaVersion = step.to. The first real step would leave inactive profiles unmigrated for good. SCHEMA_STEPS (:34) is empty, so nothing reaches this today. savedvariables-§1 requires the runner but does not spell out per-profile iteration, so this is a latent correctness trap rather than a standards breach. Low or Info are both defensible, and I keep Low. The remediation is sound, and its fallback handles the non-AceDB path (:25-26 builds NS.db without profiles). The unit case needs a test seam to inject a step, because SCHEMA_STEPS is a file-local.

findings.title: Movable named holder and stand-in frames are not excluded from the client's layout cache
findings.evidence: StartMoving marks a frame as user-placed, so the client persists its position in layout-local.txt beside the addon's own stored position. After Reset position, the two can disagree. Not verified in the client.
findings.remediation: Optional hygiene (C-008 / T-11): add a presence-guarded `if frame.SetDontSavePosition then frame:SetDontSavePosition(true) end` after holder:SetMovable (Anchor.lua:257) and f:SetMovable (StandIn.lua:153), so the client stops writing cache entries the addon always overrides. Verify in-game only by checking layout-local.txt, since the visible position is already the addon's. Cite no standards clause, because none requires it.
findings.verify_reason: It is true that the holder (modules/Anchor.lua:231, named, SetMovable at :257, StartMoving at :261/:271) and the stand-in (modules/StandIn.lua:152-158, named, StartMoving) never call SetDontSavePosition, so the client may cache them in layout-local.txt. The reachable impact is essentially nil. Both frames are re-anchored explicitly by the addon from its own stored or default position: holder:ClearAllPoints/SetPoint at Anchor.lua:101-102, and f:ClearAllPoints plus SetPoint at the stored or center position around StandIn.lua:198-206. Any cached client position is overwritten when the addon applies its layout. The finding itself says it is not verified in the client, and the 'compat' rule_ref names no clause that requires SetDontSavePosition (a grep of the standard finds no mention). This is hygiene, so Info, not Low.

findings.title: Session-long event registrations bypass the per-feature syncEvents discipline, and debug arguments are built even with debug off
findings.evidence: PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and RAID_TARGET_UPDATE are registered at file load for every enabled session, including solo and feature-off. Preview's PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED stays registered while not previewing. UnitName(...) is called just to build an NS.Debug argument on every UNIT_TARGET/UNIT_PET, even with debug off.
findings.remediation: C-008 / T-12, after T-1 and T-5: guard the NS.Debug argument construction with `if NS.State.debug`. Move PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and RAID_TARGET_UPDATE into each module's syncEvents (feature on and in a party). Move Preview's PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED into listen(on). Re-run test_disabled and confirm R_on is still non-empty.
findings.verify_reason: modules/TargetFrames.lua:320 and :326 register PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and RAID_TARGET_UPDATE on the module's bus target at file load, outside syncEvents (:208). Preview.lua:154 registers PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED unconditionally, while listen(on) at :79 gates only GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE. TargetFrames.lua:205 and PetFrames.lua:83 evaluate UnitName(btn.token) as an NS.Debug argument on every event, with debug on or off. When the whole addon is disabled the bus unregisters, so the cost is limited to the feature-off, solo and not-previewing cases, where handlers early-return. That is a small dispatch cost, so low is right. The rule_ref is loose: events-frames-taint-§1 is not a dispatch-cost rule, and the performance section would be a better citation. The remediation is sound.

findings.title: The package ships three PNG screenshots the client cannot load, and their filenames are misspelled

findings.verify_reason: .pkgmeta ignores media/logos/*.png and *.jpg but not media/screenshots. media/screenshots/ holds partframeenhanced.screenshot.0{1,2,3}.png, which is the misspelling described. README.md:27-35 links the forgecdn copies, and nothing in the code references the local files, so they are dead weight in the package. Ignoring the folder is the right fix.

findings.title: Eight container frames the addon owns (five fade frames, three free-placement holders) stay shown while it is disabled
findings.evidence: `f = CreateFrame("Frame", "PartyFrameEnhanced_Fade_" .. unit, UIParent)` carries the comment 'never hidden'. The holders are never hidden on any path either. The frames are empty and take no mouse, so nothing is visible, but the MUST says every owned frame is hidden. The suite cannot see this because the kit mock creates frames hidden.
findings.remediation: Audit Sprint 1.5: RangeFade:Suspend/Resume hides and shows the fade frames, and a new Anchor:Suspend/Resume does the same for the holders, both through NS.RunSecure because they parent or anchor secure buttons. An in-combat stand-down defers to the PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED flush. Stand-up shows the frames before PublishVisibility. Add explicit step-5 assertions that PartyFrameEnhanced_Fade_* and *_Holder are hidden after disable. Verify in game that an in-combat disable hides them once combat ends.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (Every frame the addon owns is hidden)
findings.verify_reason: RangeFade.lua:10 says fade frames are 'never hidden', and :55 creates them with CreateFrame against UIParent. Anchor.lua:232 creates the holders, and only their plate, label and grip children are ever hidden (:239-315), never the holder itself. slash-commands.md:185 says 'Every frame the addon owns is hidden', and conformance step 5 (:280) tests it. tests/test_disabled.lua has no Fade_ or Holder assertion. Nothing is visible, so low is right. Routing hides through RunSecure is prudent because secure buttons are parented to the fade frames. Driving the hide from the Suspend/Resume stand-down path is consistent with the 'at the source' requirement.

findings.title: The test kit's mock CreateFrame starts frames hidden, whereas the client starts them shown, so consumers' F_on baselines never see container frames
findings.evidence: `local f = { __shown = false, __scripts = {} }`, so a mock frame starts hidden while a client frame starts shown.
findings.remediation: Audit Sprint 5.1: in LibKa0s testkit/mock_base.lua, make CreateFrame start frames shown, as the client does. Bump the kit revision, then re-vendor tests/_kit whole into every consumer. Until then, keep the direct step-5 assertions in the addon.
findings.verify_reason: LibKa0s/testkit/mock_base.lua:121 (vendored at tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:121) has `local f = { __shown = false, __scripts = {} }`, while a real client frame starts shown. As a result, F_on never contains a frame that was created and never explicitly shown. The routing is correct: fix it upstream, bump the kit revision, then re-vendor. Flipping the default will change F_on in every consumer and may redden other addons' step-5 checks, so the upstream change should be sequenced with a collection-wide test run.

findings.title: Event registrations are bare loops with no per-event pcall, no C_EventUtils.IsEventValid gate and no record of rejected names
findings.locations: core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:140; modules/CastBars.lua:336; modules/Providers.lua:330-336; modules/PetFrames.lua:103-107; modules/TargetFrames.lua:214,320,326; modules/RangeFade.lua:168; modules/Preview.lua:81,154
findings.evidence: `for event, method in pairs(LIFECYCLE_EVENTS) do self:RegisterEvent(event, method) end` and `for i = 1, #EVENTS do el:RegisterUnitEvent(EVENTS[i], unit) end`. `grep IsEventValid` finds nothing. One retired event name would leave every later event in the block unregistered. This is latent: every name is valid on 12.1.0. Two MUSTs and one SHOULD fail.
findings.remediation: Add NS.SafeRegister in core/: one pcall per event, rejected names recorded in NS.RejectedEvents, and IsEventValid as an optional front gate that is never the only guard. Route every RegisterEvent and RegisterUnitEvent site through it. Make NS.RejectedEvents reachable through the reserved debug verb or the debug console, as §1 requires; /pfe status can also show it. Write the test first using the kit's existing M.__badEvents. Record the probing trade-off in the quirks doc. Optionally raise upstream whether LibKa0s should ship this helper, since five repos have each written their own.
findings.verify_reason: This is real. core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:140 is a bare pairs loop over RegisterEvent, CastBars.lua:336 is a bare RegisterUnitEvent loop, and there is no IsEventValid, pcall or rejected-name record anywhere outside libs/. events-frames-taint.md:30-31 sets two MUSTs: survive one bad name through a pcalled helper, and record the rejects where the player can reach them. The evidence overstates one point. The IsEventValid bullet (:32) is a SHOULD only for 'a name newer than the clients it supports', and every name here is long-established, so that SHOULD does not currently bind. Two MUSTs fail, not two MUSTs and one SHOULD. The gate is still a reasonable addition. The kit already supports the proposed test: LibKa0s testkit mock_base.lua:715-727 implements M.__badEvents. LibKa0s has no shared SafeRegister helper, so a local core/ helper is the right routing.

findings.title: The deviation register's only row (events-frames-taint-§1) is stale; v2.63.0 ruled it is not a violation

findings.title: The addon reads EllesmereUI's SavedVariables (EllesmereUIDB) to size the preview stand-in, which library-stack-§6 forbids
findings.evidence: ellesmereConfiguredSize() reads EllesmereUIDB.profiles[active].addons.EllesmereUIRaidFrames.partyFrameWidth/Height. The read is nil-guarded and read-only, and it is reached only while unlocked out of a party. There is no register row. This needs the owner's decision.
findings.remediation: Owner decision (Sprint 3.4): (a) stop the read, measuring from ERFPartyHeader's child with FALLBACK.ellesmere (125x60) as the fallback; or (b) keep it and add a library-stack-§6 register row with the trigger 'EllesmereUI exposes its configured party size through a frame or API, or its hidden party buttons report party size'. If (b) is chosen, optionally ask WowAddonStandards (Sprint 5.4) whether a presence-guarded, read-only suite SV read under §6's MAY should be permitted by name.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Providers.lua:292-302 ellesmereConfiguredSize() reads EllesmereUIDB.profiles[activeProfile].addons.EllesmereUIRaidFrames.partyFrameWidth/Height. library-stack.md:68 (§6) says a Ka0s addon 'MUST NOT read a suite's media files, textures, fonts, or SavedVariables'. Asking the owner to decide between options (a) and (b) is appropriate.

findings.title: The TOC load-order comment names the wrong file: LifecycleSetup's load-bearing position (Perf needs NS.lifecycle) is unannotated and unpinned

findings.title: The doc set lags the code at seven sites (recurring, with new content)

ARCHITECTURE.md:140 says 'The ruling narrows the *slash* surface', the v2.56.0 reasoning that v2.57.0 reversed (slash-commands.md:37). defaults/Profile.lua:4 mentions 'the phase that builds each feature'. findings.title: The AUDIT.md re-vendor check's git log --since="$horizon" skips same-day re-vendor commits
findings.evidence: git reads a bare date as the current time of day. A run at 20:00 skipped e331135, committed at 14:53 the same day. The audit read the commit directly instead. This is not a finding against the addon.
findings.remediation: Audit Sprint 5.3: in WowAddonStandards AUDIT.md, change the check to `git log --since="$horizon 00:00"`.
findings.verify_reason: WowAddonStandards/AUDIT.md:306 runs `git log --since="$horizon"`, and $horizon is a bare YYYY-MM-DD cut from the bundle name. git's approxidate fills in the current time of day for a bare date, so a commit from earlier that same day is skipped. The routing to WowAddonStandards is correct, and appending ' 00:00' fixes it.
